## The Complete Guide to Sit Stand Desks

A sit stand desk lets you switch between sitting and standing in seconds, and that flexibility is the whole point. Standing all day is no better than sitting all day; the benefit comes from changing position often. This guide explains how to choose a desk, which accessories matter, and how to arrange everything once it arrives.

## Three Types to Consider

You have a few options. A full sit stand frame with a motor is the most comfortable and the most expensive. A sit stand converter perches on top of an ordinary desk and lifts only the monitor and keyboard, which is cheaper but cramped. A manual crank desk is the budget option and works well if you only change height a couple of times a day.

## Choosing the Frame

Look for a dual motor frame with a rated capacity above 250 pounds and a height range that covers both your sitting and standing elbow height. Check the noise level while the desk moves and whether the frame wobbles at full height. We like the Flexispot and the Vari, and, if money is no object, Herman Miller. Our testing found that the cheapest frames wobble badly above 40 inches.

## Cable Management

Cable management is the difference between a desk that looks good and one that looks like a mess. Because the desk moves, every cord needs slack. Attach a surge protector to the underside of the top, use a tray, and bundle cords with reusable straps. Cable management protects your monitor too when the desk goes up quickly.

## Desk Surface

A top measuring 60 by 30 inches has room for two screens and a laptop. Bamboo and laminate are the common choices; laminate resists scratches and costs less, while bamboo looks warmer. Measure your room before you order and keep the frame clear of shelves as it rises.

## Arranging Your Desk

Adjust the top to elbow height for sitting and again for standing, then store both positions on the keypad. Put the monitor at eye level. Keep the keyboard and mouse close together so your wrists stay neutral. A sit stand routine works best when you change position every hour.

## Verdict

A good desk with a dual motor frame costs between 300 and 700 dollars and lasts for years. Add a tray, change position often, and your back will thank you.
